transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… I’m having trouble stopping myself from checking my work. Spreadsheets, calculations, that kind of thing. I’ll go over them again and again, even after I know I already checked.

Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone leaves. It feels like if I don’t check just one more time, something bad could happen, and it would be my fault.
Do you find yourself repeating these checking behaviors in other areas of your life, outside of work?

Mostly it’s at work. The spreadsheets and calculations… I just keep going back over them, even when I already checked. I can stay late for hours because it feels like if I don’t check one more time, something bad could happen and it’d be my fault.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yeah… I do. It’s usually this thought that I must have missed something, even when the numbers match. Like in payroll or taxes… that one hidden mistake is there and someone’s check won’t go through, or the firm gets in trouble.

I try to just ignore it, but it comes back. It’s like I can’t really trust what I saw.
Do you have any physical habits or actions that you feel compelled to perform over and over?

Mostly the checking. I keep going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations… again and again. Even after I already know I checked them.

Sometimes I stay for hours after everyone leaves, because it feels like if I don’t do it one more time, something bad could happen… and it’d be my fault.
Do you feel like these checking behaviors are interfering with your life outside of work or causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah… it is. I don’t really like saying that, but I missed a filing deadline because I couldn’t get out of the checking, and they called me into a formal meeting about it.

And outside work… I’ve stopped making it to choir rehearsals and things I said I’d do at the youth center, because I’m still stuck at the office. It’s… embarrassing.
Are you feeling anxious or uncomfortable when you are not able to perform your checking behaviors?

Yeah… I get really uncomfortable. If I’m not able to check again, it just sits there in my head, like something bad is going to happen and it’ll be on me.

So I end up going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations, even when I already checked them. Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone else leaves because I can’t let it go.
Do you ever feel like you have to think certain thoughts or repeat certain phrases to yourself to try and calm your anxiety about making mistakes?

Not really phrases, no. It’s more… I feel like I have to check the spreadsheets or calculations again. If I don’t, I can’t calm down, because it feels like something bad could happen and it would be my fault.
Do these thoughts about missing something in your work feel like they are coming from outside your own thinking, or are they more like your own worries?

They feel like my own worries, I guess. Not like… a voice or anything outside me.

It’s more that even when the numbers match, this thought jumps in that I missed something hidden, like in payroll or taxes, and then I can’t really trust that I saw it right. I try to push it away, but it just comes back.
Are these worries about missing something or making mistakes mostly limited to your work, or do they also happen in other areas of your life?

Mostly work, I think. Like with the payroll and tax stuff… even when the numbers match, I keep thinking maybe there’s one mistake I didn’t catch, and someone’s check won’t go through or the firm will get in trouble.

I try to tell myself it’s fine, but it just comes back. Like I can’t trust what I’m seeing.
Are you finding it difficult to maintain relationships with friends and family due to the time you spend on checking behaviors?

Yeah… I guess so. I haven’t really been making it to choir rehearsals or some youth-center things because I can’t leave the office on time.

And… I missed a filing deadline once and got called into a formal meeting at work, so it’s not just personal stuff. It’s been affecting things.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are also motivated by a need to make sure things are symmetrical or 'just right', beyond just avoiding mistakes?

Um… I don’t think so. Not really like symmetrical or needing it to look a certain way.

It’s more… I’m worried I missed something. But I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Do you feel like you're checking because you're afraid of what might happen if you make a mistake, or because you feel like you need to be in control of everything?

I think… more because I’m scared of what happens if I’m wrong.

Like, I keep going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations, even after I already checked them. If I don’t look one more time, it feels like something bad could happen and it would be my fault. Sometimes I stay hours after everyone else leaves because I can’t let it go.
Is your need to check things repeatedly more about being in control of the situation or avoiding the possibility of making an error?

It’s more about not making an error, I think.

I don’t really feel like I’m trying to control everything… it’s just, if I don’t check the spreadsheet or the calculation one more time, I get this feeling that something bad will happen and it’ll be on me. So I keep going back over it, even after I already checked. Sometimes I end up staying really late because I can’t stop.
Do you feel like your checking is driven more by the fear of something bad happening if you make a mistake, or by the need to make sure everything is perfect?

More the fear of something bad happening if I made a mistake.

It’s not really about perfect, exactly… I just keep thinking I missed something in the spreadsheet or the calculation. Even if I already checked it, I feel like I have to go back again, or it’ll be my fault if something goes wrong. Sometimes I’m there for hours after everyone else leaves.
Is your need to check things repeatedly driven by the possibility that you might have made a mistake, rather than the desire to ensure everything is perfect?

Yeah… I think it’s more that I might’ve made a mistake.

I’m not really trying to make it perfect. I just keep going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations because if I don’t check one more time, it feels like something bad could happen and it would be my fault. Sometimes I stay at work for hours after everyone else leaves because I can’t stop.
Are you feeling like your checking behaviors are significantly affecting your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Yeah… it has. I missed a filing deadline, and I got called into a formal meeting about it at work.

And I’ve been missing things outside of work too… choir rehearsals, and commitments at the youth center, because I just can’t get out of the office on time.
Do you feel like the distress from not being able to check is overwhelming at times?

Yes… it can feel really overwhelming.

If I try to leave without checking again, I just keep thinking something bad is going to happen and it’ll be my fault. I know I already checked, but it doesn’t really feel like enough. Sometimes I end up staying for hours because I can’t make myself stop.
Are there any other areas of your life, besides work and the activities you've mentioned, that are being affected by your need to check things repeatedly?

Not really… not that I can think of.

It’s mostly work, and then missing choir and the youth-center stuff because I can’t leave the office on time. That’s the main thing.
Do you think your checking behaviors are causing problems in your relationships with family or friends?

I don’t think so… not really.

I mean, I haven’t noticed it causing problems with family or friends. It’s mostly been the work stuff.
